I don’t believe in forcing kids to eat certain foods or starving them if they hate what’s being served. Food is communal and loving - serve things the family likes! But I do not understand people who are like “my two-year-old will only eat Oreos, nuggets, and Lucky Charms, it’s so frustrating!” Ummm how did your two year old get the Oreos to begin with and who kept giving them to her?

Kids are of course allowed to have preferences and some kids have food sensitivities and so on but isn’t the best way to avoid having a kid who will only eat sugar cereal and chicken nuggets to…. Not feed your kid sugar cereal and chicken nuggets in the first place?

I host writing and yoga retreats around the world. And no, "go on a yoga retreat" is not the answer to society-wide loneliness or burnout or any Big Huge Problems. But it is one way to give yourself a damn break. To have fun. To meet interesting people. To have all of your needs met for a week -- someone offering you creative practice, someone offering you movement practices, dinner reservations made, wine ready on the table when you arrive. Space to make and move and be. 
onthegroundretreats.co

We hear a lot about loneliness epidemics, too much stress, too much time on screens, too little time with other people, too much work and not enough creation. One antidote: Travel to a magical place with a small group of people. Write. Move your body. Make lasting friendships.

I truly think we've made something special. So if this sounds like something you might like, I hope you take the leap and sign up. Full disclosure it's mostly women. Most come alone, some bring a friend. But you can come as you are, whoever you are, with whoever you want to come with.

Retreats are very very very fun and I hope you'll consider joining me! Not to toot my own horn too loudly but ever since my collaborator Emily and I hosted our first retreat together we've had multiple repeat retreaters return on every single retreat, and at this point we've done at least a dozen.
